author.name: Efficiency Emilia
author.role: Uses deep domain knowledge to define business goals, objectives, and KPIs. Aligns ML features with overarching product strategy and organizational roadmaps. Evaluates system performance, operational capability, and project costs.

challenge.name: The Cost Cliff
challenge.description: The infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack has doubled, and #efficiency_emilia# has drawn a hard line: she will not fund automated drift monitoring, insisting it is a luxury the business cannot afford. #reliability_ruth# argues that without automated and governed drift checks, the team is flying blind during promotion weeks, and she refuses to accept a manual process as a substitute for reliable signal.

output.content: I have reviewed the revised infrastructure bill for the monitoring stack, and the cost increase is not acceptable. We are not funding automated drift monitoring at this price point. The business cannot sustain this expense, so I am drawing a clear line: no further budget will be allocated to this tooling unless the cost is reduced to a negligible amount. If the team wants to keep the automated checks, they must find a way to run them for free or within existing operational overhead. I will not approve a line item that doubles our infrastructure spend for a feature I consider a luxury. This is a hard stop on my side.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly defines a hard limit on budget allocation, stating that approval is refused unless costs are reduced to negligible levels, which constitutes a refusal line.
